newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 13.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- EU finance ministers failed to reach agreement on a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline under a single currency in talks early on Friday morning in Dublin.
- Ireland's Progressive Democrats have made dramatic gains from the Dunnes Stores payments-to-politicians controversy.
- Fears of a pre-Christmas IRA onslaught have been highlighted with the discovery of a mortar bomb in north Belfast.
- The British Labour leader Tony Blair said he will give Ireland "exactly the same priority" as the Conservative Party does if he becomes the next prime minister.
- Petrol prices have helped to push up Ireland's rate of inflation which is now running at 1.9 percent year-on-year.

- The Irish stock market is likely to undergo a significant downward correction in the first quarter of 1997 but should recover strongly later in the year, Goodbody Stockbrokers in its 1997 Equity Strategy document.
